newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Bunds and futures cheered by U.S. gains.
newsitem.headline: German Bunds and futures cheered by U.S. gains.

text.p: German Bunds and futures sprinted higher in late afternoon trade, mimicking a strong performance in U.S. Treasuries after soft inflation data.

Traders said the market, which had been firm but relatively subdued in the first part of the session, was ignoring domestic EMU worries for now and would continue to take its lead from U.S. credit markets in the short term.
"We had some very bullish figures from the U.S., and so Treasuries pushed up and pulled European markets with them," said one futures dealer in Frankfurt.
By 1411 GMT, the September DTB Bund future was trading 51 basis points higher at 101.27, having plotted a range from 100.70 and 101.31.
In the cash market, the 10-year benchmark Bund was at 102.00 for bid yield of 5.725 percent.
Earlier, data showing May retail sales fell 0.1 percent in the U.S. boosted Treasuries, dampening speculation on an immiment interest rate rise by the Federal Reserve.
Although the Bundesbank made a soothing statement on plans to revalue central bank reserves, traders said it was the U.S. market's move which was the driving force for Bunds.

"The Bundesbank said nothing of any importance in its statement," said one. "In the morning they left all rates unchanged, and on the revaluation of reserves, they still have not said anything very big."

The central bank, which last week forced the government to back down from plans to revalue reserves and take a one-off payment to help Germnany meet entry rules for monetary union, said it hoped a compromise solution could be reached soon.
Traders said that unless more definitive news emerged at home, Bunds would continue to follow U.S. Treasuries in the near-term.

U.S. producer prices (PPI) data for May, as well as the preliminary Michigan survey, are due on Friday. Analysts polled by Reuters are forecasting a 0.1 percent rise in PPI compared with a 0.6 percent fall in April.
But some said the chances were that after Thursday's sales data, PPI may also come in below expectations.
"If tomorrow's numbers are (bond) bullish again, we could see the Bund future going to at least 101.50," said a trader.
On the downside, if the numbers are less encouraging for debt investors, he pointed to support for September Bunds at 101.00 and then 100.90.
